interest: Tracking suspected Philippine collaborators after liberation, including 'Manila Rose'.
overview: This file consists of State Department records, FBI reports, incoming telegrams, transmittal memoranda, and a memorandum of conversation from April 1945 to January 1946 regarding wartime collaboration with Japanese occupation forces in the Philippine Islands. The documents detail intelligence reports on prominent Filipino and Spanish-Filipino political and landed elites in Iloilo who cooperated with Japanese authorities, notifications from U.S. Army Counter Intelligence concerning suspected collaborators (including individuals suspected of being propaganda broadcaster 'Manila Rose' and others) en route by ship to the United States, inter-agency transmittals to the FBI and Immigration and Naturalization Service, and an interview with an American woman previously detained in Manila on collaboration charges who sought war damage compensation while inquiring about departmental blacklists.
